title: Remediate crypto dependency chain, strengthen SAML validation, and rotate keys
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Background: A quarterly SBOM scan and external security audit flagged multiple transitive vulnerabilities affecting our auth stack: an OpenSSL CVE impacting TLS renegotiation in legacy builds, a JWT library token-parsing flaw that could lead to alg=none-like bypasses in edge cases, and an XML canonicalization/validation gap in our SAML assertion handling (xmlsec bindings). These are exploitable in aggregate for session confusion or forged assertions against older clients and on-prem agents.

Goal: Remove high/critical CVEs from our production dependency chain, harden SAML signature validation and canonicalization, rotate keys used for runtime signing where required, and validate performance/regressions across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: No open high/critical CVEs from the flagged list in the production SBOM after dependency bumps
Full CI (unit + integration + e2e SSO flows) green for hosted/dedicated/private images
Canary rollout shows <= 5% median token-generation latency regression and no error-rate increase
SAML assertion validation rejects manipulated XML inputs in fuzz suite and test harness
All signing/verification keys rotated (per key-rotation playbook) and rotation documented
Security team approval (signed off in Confluence) attached to ticket
plan: Inventory: consolidate list of vulnerable transitive deps via SBOM and OSS index (done 2026-02-21)
Upgrade plan: select target safe versions: OpenSSL -> 3.1.x-stable, JWT lib -> latest secure minor with strict alg enforcement, xmlsec bindings -> patched release
Compatibility work: run integration tests and update internal wrappers that assume previous API behavior (JWT header parsing, TLS options)
SAML hardening: add strict XML canonicalization, enforce signed root element and signed attributes, add policy-based rejection for unexpected namespaces
Key rotation: schedule rotation window with infra, update KMS policies, produce migration job for existing session tokens where applicable
Performance validation: run perf harness for token and chat endpoints and compare pre/post metrics
Canary: deploy to 3% of hosted traffic, monitor errors and latency for 48h, rollback if thresholds exceeded
Release: merge PRs, attach SBOM, update runtime-1.20 release notes and runbooks

notes: Risk: OpenSSL ABI changes may affect third-party native plugins used by private on-prem agents. We will build compatibility images and require customers on older agents to upgrade or opt into legacy TLS profile.
Mitigation: Add e2e smoke tests that run against packaged on-prem agent in staging prior to general rollout.
Follow-ups: Add automated SBOM gating to the CI pipeline and a weekly scan job to alert for newly published CVEs against used versions. Create a separate ticket to add SBOM gating: ENG-14921
